questions.topic: History of Nigerian Social Studies Education
questions.stem: Before Social Studies was introduced in Nigerian schools, pupils learnt about their society mainly through separate subjects such as
options: History, Geography and Civics
Physics, Chemistry and Biology
Mathematics and Further Mathematics
Typing and Shorthand
questions.explanation: Social Studies brought together ideas that were taught separately in History, Geography and Civics.

questions.topic: History of Nigerian Social Studies Education
questions.stem: The National Policy on Education made Social Studies a core subject at the primary and junior secondary levels. This policy was first published in
questions.explanation: The National Policy on Education, first published in 1977, made Social Studies a core subject.

questions.topic: History of Nigerian Social Studies Education
questions.stem: Social Studies as a school subject first developed in
options: the Federal Republic of Nigeria
the United States of America
the Republic of Ghana
the Empire of Japan
questions.explanation: The subject called Social Studies first developed in the USA in the early twentieth century before spreading to Africa.

questions.topic: History of Nigerian Social Studies Education
questions.stem: Which of these was a major reason for introducing Social Studies after independence?
options: Nigerian students did not like Mathematics and wanted an easier subject in schools
There were too many teachers in Nigeria who needed a new subject to teach after 1960
The colonial curriculum did not reflect the needs and values of Nigerian society
The colonial government asked for it before leaving, as a condition for independence
questions.explanation: Educators wanted a subject that would reflect Nigerian society and build citizens who could solve Nigerian problems.

questions.topic: History of Nigerian Social Studies Education
questions.stem: Social Studies is described as an integrated subject because it
options: is taught only in the evening, after the other subjects of the day have been covered
is learnt only from one textbook written by the ministry of education for all schools
combines ideas from several subjects such as History, Geography, Economics and Civics
is about numbers only, which are used to compare the populations of different places
questions.explanation: Social Studies integrates knowledge from many social sciences to study human beings and their environment.

questions.topic: History of Nigerian Social Studies Education
questions.stem: The 1969 National Curriculum Conference is important in the history of Social Studies in Nigeria because it
options: abolished all secondary schools
introduced Social Studies into universities only
banned the teaching of History
recommended a new curriculum suited to the needs of Nigerian society
questions.explanation: The conference recommended a national, relevant curriculum, which encouraged the spread of Social Studies.

questions.stem: Social Studies encourages learners to take part in voting, community work and obeying laws. This prepares them for
options: idleness
responsible citizenship
examination malpractice
tribal conflict
questions.explanation: One general objective of Social Studies is to produce responsible citizens who participate in the life of the community.

questions.stem: Social Studies helps learners to inculcate the right values. "Inculcate" here means
options: instil or teach firmly
remove or take away completely
forget or ignore totally
punish or scold severely
questions.explanation: To inculcate is to instil ideas or values firmly through repeated teaching.

questions.stem: A student who joins a clean-up exercise in his community after a Social Studies lesson on sanitation is showing that Social Studies helps learners to
options: avoid their community until all the work is done
contribute to the development of their society
become selfish about the things that they have learnt
stop going to school in order to work in the community
questions.explanation: Social Studies aims to make learners active contributors to the development of their environment.

questions.stem: National unity as an objective of Social Studies is best achieved when students
options: learn only about their own town and the history of its leaders
make fun of other cultures in order to show that theirs is the best
learn to appreciate and respect people of other ethnic groups
refuse to work with others who do not speak the same language
questions.explanation: Learning about and respecting other groups promotes national consciousness and unity.

questions.stem: Adapting to a changing environment means that a person
options: refuses any change and keeps to his or her old ways
moves house every week to avoid new problems
ignores problems until they go away on their own
adjusts well to new situations and challenges
questions.explanation: Social Studies prepares learners to cope with changes in their physical and social environment.

questions.stem: A student who learns how to resolve a quarrel between friends through dialogue has acquired which objective of Social Studies?
options: Development of skills for solving social problems
Knowledge of chemical reactions in the human body
Skills in arithmetic for sharing things equally among friends
Love for fashion and for keeping up with one's friends
questions.explanation: Social Studies develops social skills such as problem-solving, cooperation and conflict resolution.

questions.stem: Social Studies teaches students to love and be loyal to their country. This is known as
options: tribalism
nepotism
favouritism
patriotism
questions.explanation: Patriotism is love for and loyalty to one's country, which Social Studies encourages.

questions.stem: Which of these attitudes does Social Studies seek to develop in learners?
options: Hatred for other groups and their ways
Tolerance and respect for others
Laziness
Dishonesty
questions.explanation: Social Studies aims to inculcate positive attitudes such as tolerance, respect, honesty and hard work.

questions.stem: Which of the following shows that a student has achieved the Social Studies objective of being a good citizen?
options: He obeys school rules and helps others willingly
He destroys school property
He refuses to vote when he comes of age
He cheats in examinations
questions.explanation: A good citizen obeys rules, respects others and contributes positively to society.

questions.stem: Through Social Studies, learners come to understand the relationship between human beings and their
options: mobile phones only, and other modern devices
favourite music only, and the words of songs
physical and social environment
dreams about the future and their careers
questions.explanation: Social Studies studies people in relation to their physical and social environment.

questions.stem: Why is national consciousness important for a country with many ethnic groups such as Nigeria?
options: It makes each group see itself as a separate country
It makes citizens see themselves first as Nigerians and work together
It encourages ethnic conflict
It stops people from travelling
questions.explanation: National consciousness helps citizens think beyond their ethnic group and work for the good of the whole nation.

questions.stem: Social Studies helps learners to develop the ability to
options: think critically and make good decisions
avoid all responsibilities
speak only one language
memorise without understanding
questions.explanation: Social Studies develops critical thinking and decision-making skills for everyday life.

questions.stem: The three domains of Social Studies contents are
options: political, economic and religious
primary, secondary and tertiary
cognitive, affective and psychomotor
rural, urban and suburban
questions.explanation: Social Studies contents cover the cognitive (knowledge), affective (values and attitudes) and psychomotor (skills) domains.

questions.stem: Learning the names of the states and their capitals in Nigeria belongs to the
options: affective domain
psychomotor domain
emotional domain only
cognitive domain
questions.explanation: Facts and knowledge belong to the cognitive domain.

questions.stem: Developing respect for the national flag belongs to the
options: cognitive domain
psychomotor domain
physical domain
affective domain
questions.explanation: Feelings, values and attitudes such as respect and patriotism belong to the affective domain.

questions.stem: Learning to make a simple model of a traditional house in a Social Studies class develops the
options: affective domain
psychomotor domain
cognitive domain only
spiritual domain
questions.explanation: Practical skills involving the hands and body belong to the psychomotor domain.

questions.stem: Which of these is a value taught in Social Studies?
options: Honesty
Greed
Laziness
Cheating
questions.explanation: Social Studies teaches positive values such as honesty, cooperation and hard work.

questions.stem: Conceptualisation as part of Social Studies contents means
options: drawing pictures for fun
running races during sports
forming clear ideas about social issues
memorising lists of numbers
questions.explanation: Conceptualisation is understanding key ideas or concepts like culture, socialisation and governance.

questions.stem: A Social Studies lesson on road safety that teaches students the meaning of traffic signs, makes them care about safety and lets them practise crossing the road correctly covers
options: only the cognitive domain
only the affective domain
all three domains of learning
only the psychomotor domain
questions.explanation: Knowing signs is cognitive, caring is affective and practising crossing is psychomotor.

questions.stem: Skills learnt in Social Studies include
options: map reading and communication
chemical analysis of soil samples
computer programming
surgery
questions.explanation: Social Studies develops skills such as map reading, communication, cooperation and inquiry.

questions.stem: The smallest social unit in society is the
options: state
nation
local government
family
questions.explanation: The family is the smallest and most basic unit of society.

questions.stem: Which of these is an example of a primary group apart from the family?
options: A political party
A small circle of close childhood friends
A national trade union
A football fan club with thousands of members
questions.explanation: A small group of close friends is intimate and face-to-face, like the family, so it is a primary group.

questions.stem: Members of a primary group usually relate with one another
options: only through written letters
informally and personally
only through official meetings
only once in a lifetime
questions.explanation: Relationships in primary groups are informal, personal and continuous.

questions.stem: A family that includes grandparents, uncles, aunts and cousins in addition to parents and children is
options: a nuclear family
an age grade
a club
an extended family
questions.explanation: The extended family includes relatives beyond parents and children.

questions.stem: Which of these is a characteristic of a primary group?
options: Very large membership
Formal written rules only
Face-to-face interaction
Short-lived relationships
questions.explanation: Primary groups are small, with face-to-face, informal and lasting relationships.

questions.stem: The main responsibility of the father in a typical Nigerian family is to
options: provide for and protect the family
do nothing at home
leave all duties to the children
only watch television
questions.explanation: Fathers usually provide for the family's needs and protect members, though duties are increasingly shared.

questions.stem: In a family, grandparents often help by
options: teaching children family history, customs and values
paying all the bills of the community
making laws for the state
conducting elections
questions.explanation: Grandparents in Nigerian families often pass down family history, customs and moral lessons.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a secondary group?
options: A family
A circle of close friends
A trade union
A household
questions.explanation: Secondary groups, such as trade unions and associations, are larger and more formal, with less personal ties.

questions.stem: The family is regarded as the basic unit of society mainly because
options: families make the laws of the country through their heads and elders
society is built from families, and the family first trains the child
families conduct elections and choose the leaders of every single community
families collect taxes for the government from each of their members
questions.explanation: Every society is made up of families, and the family is where the child first learns values and behaviour.

questions.stem: The mother in the family helps to
options: make laws for the state
arrest criminals
print money
care for and train the children
questions.explanation: Mothers care for, nurture and train children, among other responsibilities.

questions.stem: Members of a primary group are bound together mainly by
options: written contracts only, signed by all the members
love, affection and shared interests
payment of salaries at the end of each month
force and threats from the strongest member
questions.explanation: Primary group ties are based on emotional bonds, love and mutual concern.

questions.topic: Consequences of Large and Small Family Sizes
questions.stem: A family with many children and limited income is likely to experience
options: too much money, since each child receives a government allowance
no responsibilities, because older children raise the younger ones
too much free time for parents, as the children do all the work
difficulty in providing food, education and health care
questions.explanation: With limited income, many children means each child may receive less food, schooling and care.

questions.topic: Consequences of Large and Small Family Sizes
questions.stem: One advantage of a large family in a farming community is that
options: there are more hands to help on the farm
there is less food to share
parents have more savings
children receive more individual attention
questions.explanation: In farming communities, more children can provide labour for farm work.

questions.topic: Consequences of Large and Small Family Sizes
questions.stem: Children in a small family are more likely to
options: drop out of school in order to help at home
suffer from malnutrition because of fussy eating
receive better attention and education
be neglected by parents who are always at work
questions.explanation: Fewer children allows parents to provide better care, education and nutrition for each child.

questions.topic: Consequences of Large and Small Family Sizes
questions.stem: Which of these is a disadvantage of a small family size?
options: Too many mouths to feed
Fewer relatives to support one another in times of need
Overcrowding in the house
High cost of school fees for many children
questions.explanation: Small families may lack the wide network of support that comes from many siblings and relatives.

questions.topic: Consequences of Large and Small Family Sizes
questions.stem: Rapid population growth caused by very large families can put pressure on
options: the number of stars visible at night
the size of the ocean
the length of the year
schools, hospitals and housing
questions.explanation: A fast-growing population increases demand for social amenities, often beyond what is available.

questions.topic: Consequences of Large and Small Family Sizes
questions.stem: How can family size affect the quality of life of an individual?
options: A large family always guarantees wealth, because every child will bring in an income
Family size has no effect on resources, because all families receive the same income
Resources shared among fewer people can provide better living standards for each person
Small families always have more children to share the work than large families do
questions.explanation: The same income shared among fewer members gives each person more resources for food, health and education.

questions.topic: Consequences of Large and Small Family Sizes
questions.stem: Which of these is an effect of large family sizes on the national economy?
options: Government spends more on social services, leaving less for development projects
Unemployment disappears, because every family supplies more workers to the economy
Every citizen becomes rich, because more people are paying taxes to the government
Demand for food falls, because children eat less and share what is in the home
questions.explanation: High population growth raises spending on services and can increase unemployment when jobs are limited.

questions.topic: Consequences of Large and Small Family Sizes
questions.stem: Family planning means
options: planning a family party to celebrate the birth of a new child
deciding the number and spacing of children a couple will have
choosing the colour of the family house and who should live in it
planning family holidays and the money to be spent on each trip
questions.explanation: Family planning helps couples decide how many children to have and when.

questions.topic: Consequences of Large and Small Family Sizes
questions.stem: A large family may lead to overcrowding at home, which can cause
options: more privacy
better ventilation
lower electricity bills
easy spread of diseases
questions.explanation: Overcrowding increases close contact and the spread of infectious diseases.

questions.topic: Consequences of Large and Small Family Sizes
questions.stem: A couple earns a low income and wants each child to be well educated. Which decision is MOST sensible for them?
options: Have as many children as possible so that they can help later
Stop sending their children to school in order to save money
Plan the number of children they can adequately care for
Depend on relatives for all expenses, including school fees
questions.explanation: Planning family size according to income allows parents to give each child good care and education.

questions.stem: The bearing of children in marriage is called
options: procreation
recreation
adoption
socialisation
questions.explanation: Procreation means producing children, one of the main purposes of marriage.

questions.stem: The type of marriage in which a man has one wife is
options: polygamy
polyandry
monogamy
divorce
questions.explanation: Monogamy is marriage between one man and one woman.

questions.stem: Marriage in which a man has more than one wife at the same time is called
options: monogamy
polygyny
courtship
engagement
questions.explanation: Polygyny, a form of polygamy, is when a man has more than one wife; it is permitted in customary and Islamic marriages in Nigeria.

questions.stem: Which of these is a social purpose of marriage?
options: It gives the couple and their children a recognised place in society
It allows people to avoid work, because the partner will provide all needs
It removes the need for friends, since the couple now have each other
It stops people from respecting elders who have not got married
questions.explanation: Marriage gives couples social status and recognition and links families together.

questions.stem: Marriage helps to link two families together. This promotes
options: conflict between the families over bride price
loneliness
poverty
unity and cooperation between the families
questions.explanation: Through marriage, two families become related, which builds unity and cooperation.

questions.stem: Growth in mutual love as a purpose of marriage means that the couple
options: stop talking to each other about money so that there are fewer quarrels
compete against each other at work and at home for the respect of others
live in separate towns so that each one can continue to work and earn more
develop deeper care, understanding and respect for each other over time
questions.explanation: Marriage provides a lasting relationship in which love, care and understanding grow.

questions.stem: A marriage conducted at a court or marriage registry according to the law is called
options: customary marriage
statutory (court) marriage
traditional festival
age grade ceremony
questions.explanation: Statutory marriage is conducted under the Marriage Act at a registry and is strictly monogamous.

questions.stem: Payment of bride price is a common feature of
options: divorce
adoption
customary (traditional) marriage
statutory marriage only
questions.explanation: Bride price is a traditional custom in many Nigerian customary marriages.

questions.stem: Which of these BEST explains how marriage helps to satisfy economic needs?
options: The couple combine their resources and efforts to provide for the home
Marriage makes the couple rich instantly through gifts from all their guests
Marriage removes the need to work, since relatives must now support the couple
Marriage means one partner owns all property and the other one has no duties
questions.explanation: Partners pool their income and labour to meet the family's needs.

questions.stem: Which of these is a condition for marriage?
options: Being in primary school
Being below 12 years
Financial readiness
Being unemployed by choice
questions.explanation: Partners should be able to provide for the family; financial readiness is a key condition.

questions.stem: Social stability as a condition for marriage means that a person
options: has a settled life and can relate well with others
changes jobs every day in order to earn more money
has no friends at all, and so has no reason to quarrel
is always fighting for what rightly belongs to him or her
questions.explanation: Socially stable people are settled and mature, and able to build good relationships.

questions.stem: Lack of readiness in marriage often leads to
options: a happier home with less responsibility
constant quarrels and instability
more savings
better care of children
questions.explanation: Couples not ready physically, emotionally or financially often quarrel and their marriages become unstable.

questions.stem: Why is it advisable for intending couples to do a medical test, including genotype tests, before marriage?
options: To decide the colour of the wedding dress
To know who is older
To get a driving licence
To know their health status and plan for healthy children
questions.explanation: Medical tests, including genotype and HIV tests, help couples make informed decisions and protect their children's health.

questions.stem: Under the Child's Rights Act, 2003, the minimum age for marriage is
options: 12 years
14 years
18 years
16 years
questions.explanation: The Child's Rights Act of 2003 sets 18 years as the minimum age of marriage. Some states have not yet adopted the Act.

questions.stem: A broken home is a home where
options: the parents have separated or divorced
the roof is leaking
the family is very large
the parents work in the same office
questions.explanation: A broken home results when parents separate or divorce, often affecting the children badly.

questions.stem: Which of these is MOST likely to happen to children from homes broken by constant fights between unprepared parents?
options: Better examination results and stronger discipline
Emotional problems and poor school performance
Increased parental attention from both of the parents
Greater family wealth and more chances for travel
questions.explanation: Children from broken homes often lack care and stability, which affects their emotions and schooling.

questions.stem: The legal ending of a marriage is called
options: wedding
courtship
engagement
divorce
questions.explanation: Divorce is the legal dissolution of a marriage.

questions.stem: The period during which two intending partners get to know each other well before marriage is called
options: courtship
divorce
separation
widowhood
questions.explanation: Courtship allows intending partners to understand each other before deciding to marry.

questions.stem: Members of a community coming together to clear a road or build a town hall without payment is called
options: mass protest
riot
communal labour
strike
questions.explanation: Communal labour is voluntary community work for the common good, a positive group behaviour.

questions.stem: Which of these is a constructive (positive) group behaviour?
options: Students destroying school property to protest poor food
Students organising a fundraising for a sick classmate
Fans fighting after a match to defend the honour of their team
A gang robbing travellers to support its own members
questions.explanation: Constructive group behaviour benefits the group and society, like supporting a sick classmate.

questions.stem: Group behaviour that leads to destruction of life and property is described as
options: constructive (positive)
patriotic (loyal)
cooperative (helpful)
destructive (negative)
questions.explanation: Destructive group behaviour harms people and property, such as riots and looting.

questions.stem: Belonging to a group gives a sense of companionship. This means members
options: live alone but send messages to one another
have friends with whom they share experiences
avoid one another outside their regular meetings
compete as enemies for the leadership of the group
questions.explanation: Companionship is friendship and fellowship gained from belonging to a group.

questions.stem: Mass action is a type of group behaviour in which
options: one person acts alone on behalf of a large group with a common purpose
only leaders act, while all the other members stay at home and wait
people sleep together in one place during a long journey or a festival
many people act together at the same time for a common purpose
questions.explanation: Mass action involves a large number of people acting together, such as mass rallies or campaigns.

questions.stem: Why can a peaceful protest be regarded as a positive group behaviour?
options: It allows people to express grievances lawfully without harming others
It always involves looting of shops, which gives food to the poor people
It is aimed at destroying property that belongs to those who wronged them
It stops all government activities permanently until the demands are met
questions.explanation: Lawful, peaceful protests let citizens draw attention to issues without violence.

questions.stem: One benefit of group membership is affiliation and status. This means that members
options: lose their identity in order to fit in with the rest
are ignored by others who are outside the group
gain a sense of belonging and recognition
become isolated from their families and old friends
questions.explanation: Being part of a group gives a sense of belonging and may raise one's status in society.

questions.stem: Which of the following benefits of group behaviour is shown when villagers join together to guard their community at night?
options: Survival and security
Power and control
Affiliation and status
Achievement in sports
questions.explanation: Acting together to protect the community provides survival and security for members.

questions.stem: A crowd that burns vehicles during a protest is showing
options: positive group behaviour
communal labour
patriotism
negative group behaviour
questions.explanation: Burning vehicles is destructive and therefore a negative group behaviour.

questions.stem: Participating in a fight as a group is a negative group behaviour because it
options: promotes friendship among fellow members
causes injury and breakdown of peace
builds the community through shared struggle
creates wealth for the winners of the fight
questions.explanation: Group fights cause injuries, deaths and destruction, and disturb peace.

questions.stem: A group can achieve power and control when members
options: quarrel among themselves until the strongest one emerges
refuse to meet and leave decisions to their opponents
unite to speak with one voice and influence decisions
act alone so that each one can reach the leaders directly
questions.explanation: United groups such as unions can influence decisions because they act together.

questions.stem: Which of these is a form of exploitation that trafficked persons may suffer?
options: Forced labour
Free education
Good medical care
Fair wages
questions.explanation: Trafficked persons are often forced into labour, domestic servitude or sexual exploitation.

questions.stem: Which of the following groups is MOST vulnerable to human trafficking?
options: Well-protected adults with good jobs
Senior government officials
Poor and uneducated children and women
Elderly retired judges
questions.explanation: Poverty, ignorance and lack of protection make children and women more vulnerable to traffickers.

questions.stem: Traffickers often deceive their victims with
options: warnings about the danger of leaving home to live with strangers
false promises of good jobs, education or travel abroad
honest information about the poor pay and hard conditions abroad
free legal advice from lawyers who know the laws of other countries
questions.explanation: Traffickers lure victims with false promises of jobs, schooling or a better life abroad.

questions.stem: Which of these is a factor responsible for the trafficking of children?
options: Good family income
Free compulsory education
Strong law enforcement
Poverty of parents
questions.explanation: Poor parents may give children to people who promise to help, not knowing they are traffickers.

questions.stem: One consequence of human trafficking on the victim is
options: better education in a foreign country
physical and emotional abuse
improved family ties
higher self-esteem
questions.explanation: Victims suffer abuse, trauma, sickness and sometimes death.

questions.stem: How does human trafficking weaken family love and influence?
options: Children are separated from their parents and lose family care and guidance
Families become closer, because the traffickers send back money every month
Parents spend more time with their children, because the traffickers pay them
Children receive better training at home, because they learn about the dangers
questions.explanation: Trafficking separates children from their families, breaking the bonds of love and parental guidance.

questions.stem: Victims of trafficking sometimes end up in a life of crime and addiction because
options: they are well cared for and want to please their masters
they attend good schools that teach them these behaviours
they are protected by the law when they commit crimes abroad
they are exposed to criminals, drugs and abuse
questions.explanation: Victims live among criminals, may be forced to use drugs and commit crimes, and may become addicted.

questions.stem: Human trafficking is a crime because it
options: helps victims get good jobs without proper papers
is approved by parents who are too poor to say no
violates the rights and dignity of the victims
improves the economy legally
questions.explanation: Trafficking treats human beings as goods, violating their rights and dignity.

questions.stem: Which of these is a sign that a child may be a victim of trafficking?
options: Attending school regularly with books provided by the family
Working long hours as a house help without schooling or pay
Living with parents and helping with light chores after school
Playing with friends after school in a safe community compound
questions.explanation: Children forced to work long hours without schooling or pay may be trafficking victims.

questions.stem: Human trafficking leads to loss of human resources because
options: victims who could have become productive citizens are exploited, injured or killed
it increases the number of educated people who leave to look for work in other countries
it creates more doctors and nurses who are trained abroad at the expense of the traffickers
it reduces unemployment by sending idle youths to well-paid jobs in foreign countries
questions.explanation: When young people are trafficked, the country loses their potential skills and contributions.

questions.stem: Moving people within Nigeria, for example from a village to a city, for forced labour is
options: not a crime because it is within Nigeria
a form of tourism
also human trafficking
legal if the victim is a child
questions.explanation: Trafficking can happen within a country (internal trafficking) as well as across borders.

questions.stem: Which of these is a way of preventing human trafficking?
options: Hiding cases of trafficking
Withdrawing children from school
Ignoring suspicious job offers
Public awareness campaigns
questions.explanation: Awareness campaigns inform people about traffickers' tricks and dangers.

questions.stem: Advocacy as a means of preventing human trafficking means
options: helping traffickers to travel with proper papers so that the police do not see them
speaking out and campaigning for policies and actions against trafficking
buying and selling children in order to return them to their parents and homes
keeping quiet about cases so that the families of victims are not put to shame
questions.explanation: Advocacy means publicly supporting and pushing for measures that prevent trafficking and protect victims.

questions.stem: Education helps to prevent human trafficking because it
options: makes people aware and gives them skills for decent jobs
makes people more ignorant of the world beyond their own town
forces children to travel abroad in search of better schools
increases poverty by taking young workers out of the farms
questions.explanation: Educated people can recognise traffickers' lies and have better chances of decent jobs.

questions.stem: Which of these BEST combines legislation and enforcement in preventing trafficking?
options: Writing songs about travel and playing them on the radio
Building more motor parks with guards at each entrance
Reducing the number of schools that teach about trafficking
Passing anti-trafficking laws and prosecuting offenders
questions.explanation: Laws only work when enforced; prosecuting traffickers under those laws deters others.

questions.stem: Before accepting a job offer abroad, a young person should
options: hand over his or her passport to the agent, who will keep it safe during the whole trip
leave without telling anyone, so that nobody can spoil the chance of getting the work
check that the agency and job are genuine with trusted adults and the authorities
pay any amount asked, because those who pay more are usually given much better jobs
questions.explanation: Verifying job offers and keeping one's documents helps prevent falling into traffickers' hands.

questions.stem: The law that established NAPTIP and deals with trafficking offences in Nigeria is the
options: Electoral Act, which also regulates the movement of persons during polls
Companies and Allied Matters Act, which governs the recruitment of labour
Trafficking in Persons (Prohibition) Enforcement and Administration Act
Land Use Act, which controls the use of land and the movement of workers
questions.explanation: NAPTIP was set up under the Trafficking in Persons (Prohibition) law, which was re-enacted as an Enforcement and Administration Act in 2015.

questions.stem: Rescued victims of trafficking should be rehabilitated mainly so that they
options: are punished for travelling
return to the traffickers
are kept away from their families forever
recover and are reintegrated into society
questions.explanation: Rehabilitation gives victims care, counselling and skills so they can return to normal life.

questions.stem: Parents can help prevent the trafficking of their children by
options: keeping their children in school and knowing where they are at all times
giving their children to any stranger who promises help
sending them to hawk late at night
ignoring strangers who approach them
questions.explanation: Supervising children and keeping them in school reduces their exposure to traffickers.

questions.stem: Customs that are handed down from generation to generation but cause harm to people are called
options: good traditional values
harmful traditional practices
cultural festivals
religious beliefs
questions.explanation: Harmful traditional practices are long-held customs that damage health, rights or wellbeing.

questions.stem: Giving out a young girl in marriage before she is mature is called
options: court (statutory) marriage
courtship before marriage
early (child) marriage
formal engagement
questions.explanation: Early or child marriage is the marriage of a girl before she is physically and emotionally mature.

questions.stem: Making a child work long hours in ways that harm the child's health and education is called
options: house chores
child labour
vocational training
scouting
questions.explanation: Child labour is work that is harmful to a child and deprives the child of schooling.

questions.stem: Which of these is a problem at childbirth that may result from early marriage?
options: Easier delivery and a faster return to normal daily work
Better health for the mother and a lower risk of infection
Twins every time, because a young mother has more eggs
Prolonged labour leading to vesico-vaginal fistula (VVF)
questions.explanation: A girl whose body is not mature may suffer obstructed labour, which can cause VVF and other complications.

questions.stem: The practice of forbidding widows from eating certain foods, shaving their heads and confining them for long periods is an example of
options: harmful widowhood rites
family planning
positive group behaviour
socialisation
questions.explanation: Some widowhood rites humiliate and harm widows and are regarded as harmful traditional practices.

questions.stem: The law in Nigeria that prohibits female genital mutilation is the
options: Land Use Act
Violence Against Persons (Prohibition) Act
Electoral Act
Companies and Allied Matters Act
questions.explanation: The Violence Against Persons (Prohibition) Act of 2015 prohibits female genital mutilation.

questions.stem: Using children to beg for alms on the street exposes them to
options: accidents, abuse and lack of education
good education from the people they meet
better nutrition than they receive at home
safe living conditions in the town centres
questions.explanation: Child beggars are exposed to danger and abuse and are deprived of schooling.

questions.stem: Denying girls the chance to go to school because of their gender mainly leads to
options: improvement of girls' health and more time for household work
higher national literacy, as boys will have more school places
better jobs for girls, who can start to earn money at an early age
loss of their potential contribution to the family and nation
questions.explanation: Uneducated girls have fewer opportunities, and the nation loses their potential skills.

questions.stem: Which of these is the BEST way to discourage harmful traditional practices without causing conflict in the community?
options: Burning the shrines of the community at night to avoid a fight
Insulting the elders publicly until they agree to abandon them
Educating community and religious leaders to lead change
Banning all cultural festivals until the harmful practices end
questions.explanation: When respected leaders understand the harm, they can help their communities change peacefully.

questions.stem: Which of these is a harmful traditional practice?
options: Naming ceremony
Greeting elders respectfully
Female circumcision
Traditional dance at festivals
questions.explanation: Female circumcision (female genital mutilation) is harmful; the others are harmless cultural practices.

questions.stem: Scarification or tribal marks made with unsterilised blades may lead to
options: better skin and a clearer complexion
faster growth and a stronger immune system
improved hearing and a sharper sense of smell
infections such as tetanus and HIV
questions.explanation: Unsterilised instruments can transmit infections like tetanus, hepatitis and HIV.

questions.stem: A child who is sent to hawk in the market instead of going to school is being deprived of the right to
options: education
vote
own a business
contest elections
questions.explanation: Every child has a right to basic education, which child labour denies.

questions.topic: Promoting Peaceful Living in Our Society
questions.stem: Living cordially with others means living
options: in constant quarrel with others
in a warm and friendly manner
in isolation from all neighbours
in fear of one's neighbours
questions.explanation: Cordial living is friendly, warm and harmonious living with others.

questions.topic: Promoting Peaceful Living in Our Society
questions.stem: Which of these promotes peaceful living in a community?
options: Spreading rumours about one's neighbours
Tolerance of other people's beliefs
Stealing from neighbours who are wealthy
Discrimination against new settlers
questions.explanation: Tolerance, respect and fairness promote peace among different groups.

questions.topic: Promoting Peaceful Living in Our Society
questions.stem: Settling a disagreement by discussion in which both sides give up something is called
options: compromise
revenge
violence
boycott
questions.explanation: Compromise is a way of resolving conflict where each side accepts less than it wanted for the sake of peace.

questions.topic: Promoting Peaceful Living in Our Society
questions.stem: A neutral third party who helps two disputing groups to reach an agreement is a
options: judge in a football match
campaigner
mediator
witness
questions.explanation: A mediator assists the parties in a dispute to find a solution acceptable to both.

questions.topic: Promoting Peaceful Living in Our Society
questions.stem: Negative peace refers to a situation in which
options: there is complete harmony and justice among all the people
people work together happily to settle their past differences
there is full development in every community in the whole country
there is no open violence but injustice and tension remain
questions.explanation: Negative or uneasy peace is the mere absence of open fighting while the causes of conflict remain.

questions.topic: Promoting Peaceful Living in Our Society
questions.stem: Which of these is necessary for positive peace in a society?
options: Use of force by the strong to keep the weak calm
Silence of the oppressed and those who complain
Social justice and respect for human rights
Military occupation of all troubled communities
questions.explanation: Positive peace exists when justice, fairness and rights are present, removing the causes of conflict.

questions.topic: Promoting Peaceful Living in Our Society
questions.stem: One importance of peace is that it
options: increases violence against those who disturb others
provides an environment for progress and development
scares away investors who benefit from instability
causes stress among leaders who must keep people calm
questions.explanation: Peace allows people to work, trade, learn and invest, which leads to development.

questions.topic: Promoting Peaceful Living in Our Society
questions.stem: Which of these is a cause of conflict in a community?
options: Disputes over land and boundaries
Peaceful dialogue
Mutual respect
Fair sharing of resources
questions.explanation: Land and boundary disputes are common causes of communal conflict in Nigeria.

questions.topic: Promoting Peaceful Living in Our Society
questions.stem: Why is dialogue preferred to violence in resolving conflicts?
options: It always favours the stronger group in the dispute or conflict
It takes no time at all and costs the two sides no money
It allows one side to dominate and so ends the quarrel quickly
It addresses the causes without loss of lives and property
questions.explanation: Dialogue resolves disputes by understanding, without the deaths and destruction violence brings.

questions.topic: Promoting Peaceful Living in Our Society
questions.stem: Peaceful co-existence among people of different religions in Nigeria is helped mainly by
options: forcing people to change religion
burning places of worship
banning religious practice
mutual respect and religious tolerance
questions.explanation: Respecting other people's right to their faith promotes peace in a multi-religious country.

questions.topic: Promoting Peaceful Living in Our Society
questions.stem: Which of the following actions by government would BEST promote lasting peace among communities?
options: Favouring one community in appointments until the others have settled
Ignoring complaints of marginalisation so that they do not grow any louder
Ensuring fair distribution of amenities and justice for all groups
Arresting only leaders of one group in order to warn all the other groups
questions.explanation: Fairness and justice remove grievances that lead to conflict.

questions.topic: Promoting Peaceful Living in Our Society
questions.stem: People are less stressed and happier when there is
options: war
peace
riots
crises
questions.explanation: Peace reduces fear and stress and allows people to enjoy their lives.

questions.stem: The people and institutions that teach individuals the values and norms of society are called
options: agents of socialization
agents of trafficking
tax agents
electoral agents
questions.explanation: Agents of socialization, such as the family, school and peers, transmit values and norms.

questions.stem: The process by which a child learns to become an acceptable member of the society begins in the
options: university
family
parliament
market
questions.explanation: Socialization begins at birth within the family, the primary agent.

questions.stem: Which agent of socialization teaches learners formal knowledge and discipline through a planned curriculum?
options: The peer group
The market
The motor park
The school
questions.explanation: The school uses a planned curriculum and rules to give knowledge, skills and discipline.

questions.stem: Peer groups can influence young people negatively when they
options: encourage drug use and truancy
encourage studying together
organise sporting activities
help each other with homework
questions.explanation: Peer groups can be positive or negative; bad peers may lead members into drugs and truancy.

questions.stem: Clubs and societies in school, such as the Debating Society, help to socialize students by
options: teaching them to cheat in a competition without being caught
stopping them from making friends outside their own classes
developing leadership, teamwork and communication skills
encouraging lateness to lessons, so that they meet after school
questions.explanation: Clubs give students opportunities to lead, cooperate and communicate.

questions.stem: Social media can be a negative agent of socialization when young people
options: use it to learn new skills and to find out about jobs and scholarships
copy harmful behaviours and believe false information they see online
use it to keep in touch with family and friends who live in distant places
read educational content and follow the pages of their schools and teachers
questions.explanation: Uncritical use of social media can spread harmful behaviour and misinformation among youths.

questions.stem: Learning the culture of one's society, such as greetings and dressing, through socialization helps to
options: destroy the culture
make culture unknown
stop children from growing
preserve and pass on the culture
questions.explanation: Socialization transmits culture from one generation to the next.

questions.stem: Re-socialization takes place when
options: a person learns new norms and values
a baby first learns to talk
a person falls asleep at night
a person celebrates a birthday
questions.explanation: Re-socialization is learning new norms to replace old ones, as when adjusting to a new culture or rehabilitation.

questions.stem: Which of these is an agent of socialization?
options: Weather and climate of the area
Rivers and other water bodies
Religious organisations
Mountains and other landforms
questions.explanation: Churches, mosques and other religious bodies teach moral values and are agents of socialization.

questions.stem: The mass media act as agents of socialization through
options: informing, educating and entertaining people
making laws on what people may watch or read
conducting elections for presenters and editors
arresting criminals who are shown on television
questions.explanation: Radio, television, newspapers and the internet inform, educate and entertain, shaping people's views.

questions.stem: Which of these is the MOST important reason why socialization is necessary for a child?
options: It makes the child physically taller and stronger than others of the same age
It helps the child to learn acceptable behaviour and fit into society
It replaces the need for food and rest during the early years of childhood
It stops the child from having friends who might teach him or her new habits
questions.explanation: Without socialization, a child would not learn language, values and behaviour needed to live in society.

questions.stem: Age grades are groups of people
options: of different ages in one family who perform the same roles in their community
who are rich and who use their money to carry out projects in the community
born within the same period who perform roles together in the community
who belong to one club in school only and who stop meeting when they graduate
questions.explanation: Age grades bring together people of similar age who take on community duties together.

questions.topic: Road Safety Club as an Agent of Socialization
questions.stem: The main aim of the Road Safety Club in schools is to
options: teach students how to drive taxis and commercial buses
sell vehicles and spare parts at low prices to members
collect road tolls from motorists who pass by the school
teach students road safety rules and safe road use
questions.explanation: The club educates members on road safety and helps them influence others to use roads safely.

questions.topic: Road Safety Club as an Agent of Socialization
questions.stem: The Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC) was established in
questions.explanation: The FRSC was established in 1988 to make Nigerian roads safer.

questions.topic: Road Safety Club as an Agent of Socialization
questions.stem: The teacher who guides and supervises a school Road Safety Club is usually called the
options: president
patron
secretary
treasurer
questions.explanation: A staff patron advises and supervises the activities of the club.

questions.topic: Road Safety Club as an Agent of Socialization
questions.stem: Membership of a school Road Safety Club is usually
options: only for students who own cars or have parents who drive them
only for teachers who hold valid driving licences
open to interested students who agree to obey its rules
only for commercial drivers who work near the school
questions.explanation: Interested students may join the club and agree to follow its rules and take part in its activities.

questions.topic: Road Safety Club as an Agent of Socialization
questions.stem: Members of the Road Safety Club can help to socialize youths by
options: organising road safety talks, drama and quiz competitions
encouraging over-speeding
teaching students to ignore traffic lights
selling helmets at high prices
questions.explanation: Through talks, drama and competitions, the club spreads road safety values among students.

questions.topic: Road Safety Club as an Agent of Socialization
questions.stem: Students in the Road Safety Club who teach their parents to use seat belts are acting as
options: agents of change in their families and communities
traffic wardens appointed by the FRSC in their town
commercial drivers with a licence to teach new users
vehicle inspectors who approve cars for use on the road
questions.explanation: Club members carry road safety messages home, changing the behaviour of others.

questions.topic: Road Safety Club as an Agent of Socialization
questions.stem: Which of these BEST explains why the Road Safety Club is regarded as an agent of socialization?
options: It sells driving licences to students so that they can drive when they become adults
It replaces the family by taking over the full training and discipline of the young ones
It conducts elections in schools so that members can learn how to run for a public office
It teaches members safe road attitudes and behaviours that they carry into adult life
questions.explanation: The club shapes the attitudes and behaviour of young people towards road use, which is socialization.

questions.topic: Road Safety Club as an Agent of Socialization
questions.stem: The elected student leader of a school Road Safety Club is usually called the
options: patron
president
principal
proprietor
questions.explanation: Students elect officers such as a president and secretary to run the club under the patron.

questions.topic: Road Safety Club as an Agent of Socialization
questions.stem: A school Road Safety Club works most closely with which government agency?
options: Nigeria Customs Service
National Population Commission
Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC)
Nigerian Meteorological Agency
questions.explanation: Road Safety Clubs are registered with and supported by the FRSC.

questions.stem: A condition that affects many people in society negatively and needs to be solved is called a
options: social club
social media
social problem
social event
questions.explanation: A social problem is an issue that affects many people adversely, such as unemployment or crime.

questions.stem: Children who roam the streets without care or schooling are part of the social problem of
options: street children (child neglect)
good parenting and child care
free education for children of all ages
family planning in rural homes
questions.explanation: Neglected children living on the streets are a social problem linked to poverty and broken homes.

questions.stem: Moving of large numbers of young people from villages to cities in search of jobs is called
options: urban-rural migration
emigration
immigration
rural-urban migration
questions.explanation: Rural-urban migration is the movement from villages to towns and cities.

questions.stem: Which of these is a cause of poverty in Nigeria?
options: Hard work and savings
Unemployment and low income
Good education
Access to credit
questions.explanation: Lack of jobs and low income are major causes of poverty.

questions.stem: Rapid rural-urban migration often leads to
options: empty cities and crowded villages
better housing for all who move in
fewer traffic jams on city roads
overcrowding and slums in cities
questions.explanation: Too many people moving to cities leads to overcrowding, slums and pressure on amenities.

questions.stem: Which of these BEST explains how corruption contributes to other social problems?
options: It creates more public amenities, because officials spend more to hide what they have taken
It reduces crime, because people who take bribes no longer need to steal from others
Funds meant for jobs, schools and hospitals are diverted, worsening poverty and unemployment
It strengthens institutions, because officers must work harder to cover up their actions
questions.explanation: When public money is stolen, essential services and jobs are not provided, worsening other problems.

questions.stem: Leaving school before completing one's education is called
options: dropping out of school
graduation from school
promotion to the next class
excursion to another town
questions.explanation: School drop-out is a social problem that limits young people's opportunities.

questions.stem: Which of these is a cause of examination malpractice?
options: Hard work throughout the term
Poor preparation for examinations
Regular studying
Good teaching by qualified staff
questions.explanation: Poor preparation and overemphasis on certificates push some students to cheat.

questions.stem: In many Nigerian cities, young people with no jobs are recruited by politicians as thugs. This shows that
options: unemployment has no effect on society
politics creates jobs for everyone
unemployment can lead to political violence
thuggery is a form of employment
questions.explanation: Idle youths are easily recruited into violence, showing how one social problem leads to another.

questions.stem: The sale of children or adults for exploitation, the use of hard drugs and cultism are all examples of
options: social problems
positive group behaviour
national symbols
agents of socialization
questions.explanation: These activities harm many people and society, so they are social problems.

questions.topic: Ways of Solving Social Problems in Nigeria
questions.stem: Which of these can help to reduce poverty in Nigeria?
options: Closing industries that do not pay their workers
Creating jobs and supporting small businesses
Increasing corruption so that more money circulates
Discouraging farming to reduce the supply of food
questions.explanation: Jobs and support for small businesses increase incomes and reduce poverty.

questions.topic: Ways of Solving Social Problems in Nigeria
questions.stem: Providing amenities such as electricity, schools and hospitals in rural areas helps to reduce
options: farming
village life
population of animals
rural-urban migration
questions.explanation: When villages have amenities, fewer people feel the need to move to cities.

questions.topic: Ways of Solving Social Problems in Nigeria
questions.stem: Which of these is a way the government can reduce insecurity in Nigeria?
options: Closing all police stations to save public funds
Equipping and training security agencies well
Ignoring reports from citizens who have no proof
Encouraging illegal arms for community self-defence
questions.explanation: Well-trained and equipped security agencies are better able to prevent and respond to crime.

questions.topic: Ways of Solving Social Problems in Nigeria
questions.stem: Vocational training helps solve unemployment because it
options: makes young people lazy, since they expect government to find them work
reduces the number of jobs that need to be done by workers in an industry
gives young people practical skills to work for themselves or others
replaces all schools, so that young people can start to earn money early
questions.explanation: Skills such as tailoring, carpentry and ICT allow people to be self-employed or employable.

questions.topic: Ways of Solving Social Problems in Nigeria
questions.stem: Individuals can help to reduce corruption by
options: refusing to give or take bribes
giving bribes to get things done quickly
covering up corrupt officials
praising stolen wealth
questions.explanation: When individuals refuse bribes, corruption becomes harder to practise.

questions.topic: Ways of Solving Social Problems in Nigeria
questions.stem: Which of these is a long-term solution to social problems in Nigeria?
options: Giving out cash only on election day
Punishing only poor offenders
Ignoring the problems
Quality education and good governance
questions.explanation: Education and good governance address the root causes of many social problems.

questions.topic: Ways of Solving Social Problems in Nigeria
questions.stem: Religious organisations can help to solve social problems by
options: encouraging hatred of those who commit crimes
promoting violence against people who do wrong
hiding criminals who show regret for their acts
teaching moral values and supporting the needy
questions.explanation: Religious bodies teach good values and often provide welfare services.

questions.topic: Ways of Solving Social Problems in Nigeria
questions.stem: A state government wants to reduce youth involvement in cultism. Which combination of measures is MOST effective?
options: Ignoring cult activities and closing sports facilities
Giving cultists money
Counselling, youth engagement programmes and firm enforcement of the law
Banning all school clubs
questions.explanation: Combining guidance, positive activities and law enforcement attacks both causes and practice of cultism.

questions.topic: Ways of Solving Social Problems in Nigeria
questions.stem: Social problems affect a country's image abroad because
options: social problems are praised abroad as signs of progress
other countries may see it as unsafe or poorly governed
foreigners do not hear about them until they visit the country
they always attract tourists who wish to see the problems
questions.explanation: Problems such as crime and corruption damage a country's reputation internationally.

questions.topic: Ways of Solving Social Problems in Nigeria
questions.stem: Non-governmental organisations (NGOs) help to solve social problems mainly by
options: running skills and health programmes
making laws for the country
conducting national elections
commanding the armed forces
questions.explanation: NGOs work with communities on education, health, rights and skills.

questions.topic: Our Roles in Promoting Safety in Our Community
questions.stem: Before using a sharp tool such as a cutlass on the school farm, a student should
options: swing it around to test it for balance and for the sharpness of its blade
learn how to handle it properly and point it away from people
throw it to a classmate to see if it is safe for both of them to use
use it while running so that the work will be completed before the bell
questions.explanation: Correct handling and keeping blades away from others prevents injuries.

questions.topic: Our Roles in Promoting Safety in Our Community
questions.stem: Children playing football on a busy road are
options: using the road correctly, provided that they keep to the left
helping traffic flow by making drivers slow down near the pitch
exposing themselves to the danger of being hit by vehicles
obeying road safety rules as long as they wear bright jerseys
questions.explanation: Roads are for vehicles and careful crossing, not play; playing on them risks being knocked down.

questions.topic: Our Roles in Promoting Safety in Our Community
questions.stem: A car driver and passengers should always
options: use their seat belts
hang out of the windows
sit on the bonnet
drive without lights at night
questions.explanation: Seat belts reduce injuries and deaths in road crashes.

questions.topic: Our Roles in Promoting Safety in Our Community
questions.stem: Keeping medicines and chemicals out of the reach of children prevents
options: drowning
road accidents
flooding
poisoning
questions.explanation: Children can mistake medicines and chemicals for food or drinks, leading to poisoning.

questions.topic: Our Roles in Promoting Safety in Our Community
questions.stem: Which of these is a safety guideline for cyclists?
options: Carry passengers on the handlebars to keep the balance steady
Ride on the correct side of the road and obey traffic signals
Ride at night without lights in order to see the road better
Hold on to moving vehicles when climbing steep hills on the road
questions.explanation: Cyclists should obey traffic rules, use lights and reflective wear, and not carry passengers unsafely.

questions.topic: Our Roles in Promoting Safety in Our Community
questions.stem: Drinking alcohol before driving is dangerous because it
options: improves concentration
makes the driver more careful
slows reactions and impairs judgement
sharpens eyesight
questions.explanation: Alcohol impairs a driver's judgement, coordination and reaction time, causing crashes.

questions.topic: Our Roles in Promoting Safety in Our Community
questions.stem: Overloading a vehicle is unsafe because it
options: makes the vehicle faster and easier to stop on hills
saves fuel by spreading the weight over all the tyres
protects the passengers by holding them firmly in place
makes the vehicle difficult to control and brake
questions.explanation: Excess weight affects steering and braking and can cause the vehicle to overturn.

questions.topic: Our Roles in Promoting Safety in Our Community
questions.stem: In a workplace, which of these BEST promotes safety?
options: Using protective equipment and following safety rules
Removing guards from machines to work faster
Working while tired and sleepy
Ignoring safety signs
questions.explanation: Personal protective equipment and safety rules reduce accidents at work.

questions.topic: Our Roles in Promoting Safety in Our Community
questions.stem: Why should electrical appliances be switched off and unplugged when not in use?
options: To prevent fire and electric shock and to save energy
To make them work faster the next time they are used
Because they become heavier if left plugged in for long
So that they do not change colour when the light falls on them
questions.explanation: Unplugging reduces the risk of electrical fires and shocks and saves energy.

questions.topic: Our Roles in Promoting Safety in Our Community
questions.stem: In school, students can promote safety by
options: playing with fire in the laboratory to learn how it behaves
running on wet floors to get to class before the bell rings
reporting broken windows, exposed wires and other hazards
climbing over the fence so as to avoid crowds at the school gate
questions.explanation: Reporting hazards allows them to be fixed before someone gets hurt.

questions.topic: Our Roles in Promoting Safety in Our Community
questions.stem: Motorists should obey speed limits mainly because
options: speed limits make journeys longer for no reason
high speed reduces control and increases the severity of crashes
speed limits are only for trucks
police like slow cars
questions.explanation: At high speed, drivers have less time to react and crashes are more serious.

questions.topic: Our Roles in Promoting Safety in Our Community
questions.stem: When a pedestrian walks along a road without a sidewalk, the safest thing is to walk
options: with one's back to oncoming traffic in the middle of the road
while wearing headphones at full volume
in a group spread across the road
facing the oncoming traffic and keeping close to the edge
questions.explanation: Facing oncoming traffic lets the pedestrian see vehicles and step aside in time.

questions.stem: Which of these is a punishment that can be given to a convicted drug trafficker in Nigeria?
options: Imprisonment
A national award
A scholarship
Free land
questions.explanation: Drug traffickers convicted in Nigeria face imprisonment and may lose their assets.

questions.stem: A person who carries hard drugs in his body or luggage across borders for traffickers is often called a
options: pharmacist
drug courier (mule)
customs officer
doctor
questions.explanation: Drug couriers carry illegal drugs for traffickers, risking their lives and arrest.

questions.stem: Ignorance contributes to drug trafficking when people
options: know the law very well
have good jobs
do not know the dangers and penalties involved
refuse to carry packages for strangers
questions.explanation: Some people are tricked into trafficking because they do not understand the risks and penalties.

questions.stem: Drug trafficking gives a country a bad image because
options: it improves tourism
it attracts honest investors
it increases exports of farm produce
its citizens may be treated with suspicion abroad
questions.explanation: When citizens are caught trafficking, others from the country face extra checks and suspicion abroad.

questions.stem: Drug couriers who swallow wrapped drugs risk
options: becoming healthier because of the drug in the body
winning an award from the customs for honest travel
death if the wrappers burst in their stomach
faster digestion that removes the drugs from the blood
questions.explanation: Burst wrappers release large amounts of drugs into the body, which can be fatal.

questions.stem: In some countries, drug trafficking is punishable by death. This shows that
options: drug trafficking is legal in those countries
drug trafficking is regarded as a very serious crime worldwide
drug traffickers are honoured there
drugs are harmless
questions.explanation: Severe penalties in many countries show how seriously drug trafficking is viewed.

questions.stem: Drug trafficking affects the economy negatively because
options: illegal money distorts the economy and drug abuse reduces the productivity of workers
it increases legal tax revenue, which governments then spend on more drug control agencies
it creates healthy workers who earn enough to support their families and communities
it reduces crime, since drug dealers keep other criminals away from their areas
questions.explanation: Drug money is not taxed and encourages crime, while drug abuse destroys productive human resources.

questions.stem: Choosing good friends helps young people to
options: start using drugs in order to fit in
drop out of school
join cults
avoid involvement in drugs
questions.explanation: Good friends encourage positive behaviour and help one resist pressure to use drugs.

questions.stem: Refusal skills help a young person to
options: accept drugs politely from older friends
say no firmly to offers of drugs
sell drugs without being found out
hide drugs from parents and teachers
questions.explanation: Refusal or resistance skills allow young people to decline drugs confidently.

questions.stem: Forming drug-free clubs in schools helps to discourage drug abuse by
options: selling drugs to members at low prices so that others cannot profit
encouraging truancy so that members stay away from drug sellers at school
making drugs cheaper to buy so that students will not need to steal
promoting healthy activities and peer support for staying drug-free
questions.explanation: Drug-free clubs give students positive peer support and healthy activities.

questions.stem: A student is being pressured by friends to carry a "small package" across town for money. Which decision-making step should come FIRST?
options: Agreeing immediately to get the money before someone else does
Opening the package in public so that others can see what is in it
Thinking about the possible consequences before acting
Asking for more money because of the risk that is involved in it
questions.explanation: Good decision-making involves considering the consequences; carrying unknown packages could involve drug trafficking.

questions.stem: Which of these would BEST discourage young people from joining drug trafficking?
options: Campaigns showing the dangers and penalties of trafficking
Films that glorify drug barons
Praising rich people whose source of wealth is unknown
Hiding information about drug laws
questions.explanation: Awareness of the dangers and penalties discourages young people from trafficking.

questions.stem: Legislation helps to prevent drug trafficking by
options: legalising all drugs so that they can be taxed and controlled
reducing the number of police who search for drug offenders
providing strict laws and punishments for offenders
encouraging drug use only in approved clinics and hospitals
questions.explanation: Laws define drug offences and set penalties that deter traffickers.

questions.stem: Alleviation of poverty helps to prevent drug trafficking because
options: people with legitimate means of livelihood are less tempted by drug money
poor people are always traffickers and they stop as soon as they find work
drug trafficking creates wealth for all members of a poor community equally
it increases the price of drugs, so that poor people can no longer afford them
questions.explanation: When people have decent incomes, they are less likely to be lured into trafficking.

questions.stem: The international community helps to prevent drug trafficking mainly by
options: allowing drugs to move freely so that they can be traced to their final destination
supporting drug barons who agree to give up their trade and invest in local business
closing all airports permanently so that no passenger can ever carry any illegal drugs
sharing information and cooperating in arresting traffickers across borders
questions.explanation: Drug trafficking crosses borders, so countries cooperate through information sharing and joint operations.

questions.stem: The United Nations body that coordinates international efforts against illicit drugs and crime is the
options: United Nations Children's Fund (UNICEF)
United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC)
Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO)
International Labour Organization (ILO)
questions.explanation: UNODC leads the UN's fight against illicit drugs and international crime.

questions.stem: Education helps to prevent drug trafficking by
options: teaching how to traffic drugs without being caught
hiding the truth about drugs from young learners
praising drug barons who give money to poor schools
making people aware of its dangers and consequences
questions.explanation: Awareness of the dangers and penalties discourages people from getting involved.

questions.stem: Forfeiture of assets as a consequence of drug trafficking means that
options: the trafficker is given more property in exchange for telling the police about his partners
property acquired with drug money, both in Nigeria and abroad, is taken by government
the trafficker's family receives compensation from the government for the property lost
the trafficker is released as soon as all the money has been paid back to the government
questions.explanation: Courts can order property bought with proceeds of drug crimes to be confiscated by the state.

questions.stem: The International Day Against Drug Abuse and Illicit Trafficking is observed every year on
options: 26th June
1st October
12th June
25th December
questions.explanation: The UN marks 26th June each year as the International Day Against Drug Abuse and Illicit Trafficking.

questions.stem: Which of these is the MOST effective way that communities can help prevent drug trafficking?
options: Protecting drug dealers from the police in return for community projects
Buying property from suspected traffickers at lower prices for the community
Reporting suspected drug dealers to the NDLEA and educating young people
Celebrating traffickers as role models who give jobs to young people in town
questions.explanation: Communities help by reporting suspects to the authorities and teaching youths about the dangers.

questions.topic: Meaning and Consequences of Drug Abuse and Harmful Substances
questions.stem: Using a drug without a doctor's prescription or in a way that harms the body is called
options: drug prescription
immunisation
drug abuse
first aid
questions.explanation: Drug abuse is the use of drugs in harmful ways or without medical direction.

questions.topic: Meaning and Consequences of Drug Abuse and Harmful Substances
questions.stem: A person who cannot stop taking a drug even when it is harming him is said to be
options: immunised (protected)
contented (satisfied)
disciplined (self-controlled)
addicted (dependent)
questions.explanation: Addiction (dependence) is the strong need to continue using a drug despite harm.

questions.topic: Meaning and Consequences of Drug Abuse and Harmful Substances
questions.stem: Inhaling glue, petrol or other chemicals to get "high" is a form of
options: solvent (inhalant) abuse
medical treatment
healthy recreation
immunisation
questions.explanation: Sniffing solvents damages the brain, lungs, liver and kidneys and can kill instantly.

questions.topic: Meaning and Consequences of Drug Abuse and Harmful Substances
questions.stem: Which of these is a consequence of drug abuse on the individual?
options: Better memory and faster learning at school
Mental illness and damage to body organs
Improved school results in most of the subjects
Stronger lungs and a more active heart
questions.explanation: Drug abuse can cause mental disorders, organ damage, addiction and death.

questions.topic: Meaning and Consequences of Drug Abuse and Harmful Substances
questions.stem: Drug abuse affects the community when abusers
options: help keep the community safe
engage in crime and violence
become more productive
promote peace
questions.explanation: Drug abuse is linked to theft, violence and insecurity in communities.

questions.topic: Meaning and Consequences of Drug Abuse and Harmful Substances
questions.stem: How does drug abuse among the youths affect the nation?
options: It increases national productivity, as young people work for longer hours in a day
It reduces crime rates, because young users stay at home and do not go out at night
It improves the health system, since more hospitals will be built for drug users
It reduces the productive workforce and increases health and security costs
questions.explanation: When youths are addicted, the nation loses productive workers and spends more on health and security.

questions.topic: Meaning and Consequences of Drug Abuse and Harmful Substances
questions.stem: Taking someone else's prescribed drug because you have similar symptoms is dangerous mainly because
options: drugs are always safe for everyone who has the same symptoms
it will cure you faster than it would cure the first person
the drug or dose may be wrong for you and cause harm
it is approved by doctors for use by all the members of a family
questions.explanation: Drugs are prescribed for a specific person and condition; wrong drugs or doses can be harmful.

questions.topic: Meaning and Consequences of Drug Abuse and Harmful Substances
questions.stem: Smoking cigarettes can cause
options: lung cancer and heart disease
stronger lungs and deeper breaths
better breathing during sports
longer life and lower stress
questions.explanation: Tobacco smoking causes lung cancer, heart disease and other illnesses.

questions.topic: Meaning and Consequences of Drug Abuse and Harmful Substances
questions.stem: Drinking too much alcohol over a long period can damage the
options: liver
fingernails only
hair only
teeth only
questions.explanation: Heavy drinking can cause liver diseases such as cirrhosis.

questions.topic: Meaning and Consequences of Drug Abuse and Harmful Substances
questions.stem: Drug abuse in Nigeria can affect the international community mainly because
options: other countries do not care about drugs as long as their own citizens are safe
drug abuse stays only within one family and does not go beyond the national borders
it improves diplomatic relations between the countries that import and export drugs
drug abuse and trafficking networks cross borders and affect other countries
questions.explanation: Drug problems spread across borders through trafficking networks, affecting many countries.

questions.stem:
(a) What is Social Studies? [2 marks]
(b) State four general objectives of Social Studies. [8 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) Social Studies is an integrated study of human beings in relation to their physical and social environment
2 marks: (b) To help learners adapt to a changing environment
2 marks: (b) To inculcate national consciousness and national unity
2 marks: (b) To produce good citizens able and willing to contribute to the development of society
2 marks: (b) To inculcate the right types of values and attitudes / to develop skills for solving social problems
questions.explanation: Social Studies studies people and their environment. Award 2 marks for each correctly stated objective.

questions.stem:
(a) Name the three domains of the contents of Social Studies. [3 marks]
(b) Explain each domain and give one example of what is learnt in it. [6 marks]
(c) Mention one value taught in Social Studies. [1 mark]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: (a) Cognitive
1 mark: (a) Affective
1 mark: (a) Psychomotor
