2 marks: (b) Cognitive: knowledge and understanding, e.g. facts about the family or government
2 marks: (b) Affective: feelings, values and attitudes, e.g. respect for others, patriotism
2 marks: (b) Psychomotor: practical skills, e.g. drawing maps, making models
1 mark: (c) Honesty / cooperation / tolerance / hard work
questions.explanation: Social Studies contents cover knowledge (cognitive), values and attitudes (affective) and skills (psychomotor).

questions.stem:
(a) What is a primary group? [2 marks]
(b) Give three reasons why the family is regarded as a primary group. [3 marks]
(c) State the responsibilities of (i) parents (ii) children in the family. [5 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) A small social group whose members have close, personal, face-to-face and lasting relationships
1 mark: (b) Members interact face to face
1 mark: (b) Members are bound by love and affection
1 mark: (b) It is the first group a child belongs to and where socialisation begins
1 mark: (c)(i) Providing food, shelter and clothing
1 mark: (c)(i) Paying school fees / caring for health
1 mark: (c)(i) Teaching good morals and values
1 mark: (c)(ii) Obeying and respecting parents
1 mark: (c)(ii) Helping with house chores / studying hard
questions.explanation: The family is a primary group because of its small size, intimacy and role in early socialisation. Accept other valid responsibilities.

questions.topic: Consequences of Large and Small Family Sizes
questions.stem:
(a) Describe a large family and a small family. [4 marks]
(b) State three consequences of large family size on the national economy. [3 marks]
(c) Give three advantages of a small family. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) Large family: father, mother and many children
2 marks: (a) Small family: father, mother and very few children
1 mark: (b) Rapid population growth and pressure on social amenities
1 mark: (b) High unemployment
1 mark: (b) More government spending on services, less for development / low savings and investment
1 mark: (c) Better care and attention for each child
1 mark: (c) Better education and nutrition
1 mark: (c) Less financial burden on parents / less overcrowding
questions.explanation: Family size affects both the quality of individual lives and the national economy. Accept other relevant points.

questions.stem:
(a) What is marriage? [2 marks]
(b) State four conditions a person should satisfy before getting married. [4 marks]
(c) Mention four effects of lack of readiness on a marriage. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) Marriage is a legally and socially recognised union between a man and a woman as husband and wife
1 mark: (b) Physical fitness / maturity
1 mark: (b) Psychological (emotional) fitness
1 mark: (b) Social stability
1 mark: (b) Financial readiness
1 mark: (c) Constant fights and instability
1 mark: (c) Divorce or separation
1 mark: (c) Broken homes
1 mark: (c) Neglect of children / children becoming delinquent
questions.explanation: Readiness for marriage includes physical, psychological, social and financial fitness. Lack of readiness causes instability, divorce and broken homes.

questions.stem:
(a) What is group behaviour? [2 marks]
(b) Distinguish between constructive and destructive group behaviour, giving one example of each. [4 marks]
(c) State four benefits of positive group behaviour. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) The way people act or behave together as members of a group
2 marks: (b) Constructive (positive): group behaviour that benefits society, e.g. communal labour
2 marks: (b) Destructive (negative): group behaviour that harms people or property, e.g. riots, looting
1 mark: (c) Companionship
1 mark: (c) Survival and security
1 mark: (c) Affiliation and status
1 mark: (c) Power and control / achievement of goals
questions.explanation: Group behaviour may be positive or negative. Benefits listed in the syllabus are companionship, survival and security, affiliation and status, power and control, and achievement.

questions.stem:
(a) What is human trafficking? [2 marks]
(b) State four factors responsible for the trafficking of children and women. [4 marks]
(c) Explain two consequences of human trafficking. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) The recruitment, transport or harbouring of people by force or deception for the purpose of exploitation
1 mark: (b) Poverty
1 mark: (b) Ignorance / illiteracy
1 mark: (b) Unemployment
1 mark: (b) Greed of traffickers and some parents / broken homes / desire to travel abroad
2 marks: (c) Loss of human resources: victims who could have contributed to national development are exploited or killed
2 marks: (c) Life of crime, addiction and sexual violence / weakening of family love and influence
questions.explanation: Trafficking exploits people through force or deception. Accept other valid factors and consequences.

questions.stem: Describe five measures that can be taken to prevent human trafficking in Nigeria. [10 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Awareness campaigns through media, schools and religious bodies
2 marks: Education of children, especially girls, and skills acquisition
2 marks: Advocacy by NGOs and community leaders against trafficking
2 marks: Legislation and strict enforcement, e.g. prosecution of traffickers by NAPTIP
2 marks: Poverty alleviation / parents supervising children / verifying job offers abroad
questions.explanation: Award 1 mark for naming each measure and 1 for describing it. Accept other valid measures.

questions.stem:
(a) What are harmful traditional practices? [2 marks]
(b) Give four examples of harmful traditional practices. [4 marks]
(c) Suggest four ways of preventing harmful traditional practices. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) Customs handed down over generations that damage the health, rights or wellbeing of people, especially women and children
1 mark: (b) Early (child) marriage
1 mark: (b) Female circumcision (FGM)
1 mark: (b) Child labour
1 mark: (b) Use of children for begging / harmful widowhood rites
1 mark: (c) Public enlightenment and education
1 mark: (c) Enforcing laws such as the Child's Rights Act and VAPP Act
1 mark: (c) Involving traditional and religious leaders
1 mark: (c) Girl-child education / support for victims
questions.explanation: Harmful practices damage health and deny rights. Prevention involves education, law enforcement and community leadership.

questions.topic: Promoting Peaceful Living in Our Society
questions.stem:
(a) Explain the meaning of peace. [2 marks]
(b) Differentiate between positive peace and negative peace. [4 marks]
(c) State four ways of promoting peace in our society. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) Peace is a state of harmony, order and friendly living without violence or conflict
2 marks: (b) Positive peace: harmony with justice, fairness and respect for rights
2 marks: (b) Negative (uneasy) peace: mere absence of open violence while tension and injustice remain
1 mark: (c) Tolerance
1 mark: (c) Social justice
1 mark: (c) Respect for human rights
1 mark: (c) Dialogue and peaceful resolution of conflicts
questions.explanation: Peace is more than absence of war; positive peace includes justice. Accept other valid ways of promoting peace.

questions.stem:
(a) What is socialization? [2 marks]
(b) List four agents of socialization. [4 marks]
(c) State four importance of socialization. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) The process by which a person learns the values, norms and culture of the society
1 mark: (b) Family
1 mark: (b) School
1 mark: (b) Peer group
1 mark: (b) Religious organisations / mass media / age grades / clubs
1 mark: (c) Transmits culture from generation to generation
1 mark: (c) Helps individuals to learn acceptable behaviour
1 mark: (c) Promotes discipline and social control
1 mark: (c) Prepares individuals for adult roles / promotes unity
questions.explanation: Socialization is lifelong learning of societal norms through agents such as the family, school, peers, religion and media.

questions.topic: Road Safety Club as an Agent of Socialization
questions.stem:
(a) Describe the steps involved in forming a Road Safety Club in a school. [6 marks]
(b) State four roles of the Road Safety Club in the socialization of youths. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) Seeking approval from the school authority and appointing a teacher as patron
2 marks: (a) Enlisting interested students as members and electing officers (president, secretary etc.)
2 marks: (a) Registering the club with the nearest FRSC office and drawing up a programme of activities
1 mark: (b) Teaching members road safety rules
1 mark: (b) Organising road safety campaigns, drama and quizzes
1 mark: (b) Developing discipline and leadership in members
1 mark: (b) Spreading safety messages to families and communities
questions.explanation: Accept equivalent steps in sensible order. The club shapes safe road use attitudes, making it an agent of socialization.

questions.topic: Our Roles in Promoting Safety in Our Community
questions.stem:
(a) Explain why safety is necessary. [2 marks]
(b) State two safety measures each in (i) the home (ii) the school. [4 marks]
(c) State two safety guidelines each for (i) pedestrians (ii) motorcyclists. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) To prevent accidents, injuries, loss of life and property
1 mark: (b)(i) Keep medicines and chemicals out of children's reach
1 mark: (b)(i) Switch off electrical appliances / handle gas safely
1 mark: (b)(ii) Report hazards such as exposed wires
1 mark: (b)(ii) Avoid running on stairs or wet floors / follow fire drills
1 mark: (c)(i) Use zebra crossings or pedestrian bridges
1 mark: (c)(i) Look both ways before crossing / walk facing oncoming traffic
1 mark: (c)(ii) Wear a crash helmet
1 mark: (c)(ii) Avoid overloading and over-speeding / obey traffic signals
questions.explanation: Accept any valid safety measures and guidelines for each setting and road user.

questions.topic: Meaning and Consequences of Drug Abuse and Harmful Substances
questions.stem:
(a) Explain the meaning of drug abuse. [2 marks]
(b) Mention four forms of drug abuse. [4 marks]
(c) Explain the consequences of drug abuse on (i) the individual (ii) the nation. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) The use of drugs without prescription, in excess, or in ways that harm the body and mind
1 mark: (b) Self-medication / overdose
1 mark: (b) Use of illegal drugs such as cannabis or cocaine
1 mark: (b) Abuse of codeine syrups or tramadol
1 mark: (b) Sniffing solvents / alcohol and tobacco abuse
2 marks: (c)(i) Individual: addiction, mental illness, damage to organs, school drop-out or death
2 marks: (c)(ii) Nation: loss of productive workforce, increased crime and insecurity, bad international image
questions.explanation: Drug abuse harms individuals, families, communities and the nation. Accept other valid forms and consequences.
